core.title: Advisory semantic anchor (not directly enforced): read and author a user/system flow as one linear end-to-end journey ending in one terminal contract
core.given: a planner is decomposing a domain into user/system flows, or interpreting/classifying an existing journey as a user/system flow
core.when: they define, reshape or classify a user/system flow
core.then: Use this advisory definition: a user/system flow names exactly one executable end-to-end journey — a strictly linear, ordered sequence of steps across declared product capabilities, from a declared initial input to exactly one terminal contract. It enforces nothing directly; the rule nodes that require it do the enforcing.
prefer: A full journey the domain can run end to end, not a fragment.
Strictly sequential steps between declared participants, with one coherent outcome, at least 2 product capabilities and ideally 3-7.
Declare the initial input and the artifacts moved from step to step.
Have the terminal step declare exactly one primary artifact, and derive the user/system flow's family from it.
avoid: Loops, routes or branching inside a user/system flow.
Bundling several journeys or outcomes into one user/system flow.
Multiple terminal contracts, or a family that disagrees with the terminal contract.
Specifying how the journey runs or what runtime state it holds; those are implementation and test concerns, not plan-artifact concerns.
Treating this anchor as a separately enforced rule. Findings come from the rule nodes that require it.
core.why: A user/system flow names WHAT journey the domain must support. This anchor gives that a stable meaning, and the enforceable nodes that require it (linearity, scope, terminal contract, family) do the checking.
evidence: This node is advisory and not bound to a validator. Compliance is established through the enforceable rule nodes that require this anchor: linearity, scope, sequence, participants, initial-input declaration, artifact flow, terminal contract, family, and family-matches-terminal-contract.
A reviewer confirms the user/system flow reads as one coherent end-to-end journey from a declared input to one terminal artifact.
verification: Advisory semantic anchor: a definitional node that gives the artifact a stable meaning. It is not itself bound to any validator and enforces nothing directly; any findings come from the enforceable rule nodes that require this anchor, which protect it transitively.

Definition the anchor provides: user/system flow = {executable, linear, single-outcome, wagon-composed, initial-input, single-terminal-contract}. The requiring rule nodes check the individual aspects; this node itself checks nothing.

Activation facts are alternative signals only, none a mandatory gate; task terms must never be used as a lexical gate, and read-only interpretation or classification counts as much as editing (no edit or shape change is required).

No established observer identifies the planning phase or user/system flow artifacts (needs_new_observer): a realization must provide one, either by an agreed plan-tree path/file-kind convention or by schema inspection (for example, an artifact declaring capabilities/steps and a terminal contract). This node defers that classification to the stack's plan-artifact conventions.

values: deciding what a user/system flow is: interpreting, classifying, defining or reshaping a journey (steps, product capabilities, initial input, terminal contract)

fires: Planner drafts a new user/system flow for an end-to-end user/system journey across product capabilities.
Planner restructures an existing user/system flow's steps, participants, initial input or terminal step.
Planner decides whether a set of product capabilities forms one user/system flow or several.
Planner interprets or classifies an existing journey as a user/system flow (or not) without editing any user/system flow file.
doesNotFire: Coder implements how a user/system flow journey runs or whether it holds runtime state.
Tester writes runtime tests for a user/system flow's execution.
Planner edits a single product capability's internals without defining, interpreting or relying on any user/system flow's meaning.

neutralityNotes: The convention is an advisory definitional anchor about plan artifacts and was already stack-neutral in substance; only the legacy sibling rule ids (planner.train.*) were realization-specific and are carried in bunOnly while the core names the enforcing concerns generically. 'Planner', 'coder' and 'tester' are workflow roles, not stack roles, so given/when and activation.fires/doesNotFire carry over essentially verbatim (fires and doesNotFire are not numbered items and are not separately classified). Because the core activation-fact shape has no note field, the notes' conditions — alternative signals only, no mandatory lexical gate, read-only interpretation counts, no edit required, and the deferred train-artifact classification — are preserved in core.verification. The file_kind=train and phase=planning signals remain needs_new_observer; once a stack establishes that observer it will need its plan root (roots.plan) and plan-artifact kinds (roles.plan_artifact.kinds) to classify train artifacts, of which only roles.plan_artifact.kinds is a requirement of this core today.
